server.name: bookdna
server.title: BookDNA
server.description: Book DNA (tropes, world, subgenre, tone) and verified reading recommendations, backed by Open Library.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Use search_book to identify a book, get_book_dna to break it into tropes, setting, subgenre, tone and storyline, recommend for one shelf of books like a given book, and recommend_by_tropes when the reader names tropes rather than a book. Every recommended book has been verified to exist on Open Library.

tool.description: Find the single best Open Library match for a book and return its title, authors, first publication year, cover URL and description. Use this to identify or confirm a book; it does not analyse or recommend. Does not use AI, so it is never rate limited.

tool.name: get_book_dna
tool.title: Get a book's DNA
tool.description: Break a book down into its DNA: 3 to 6 tropes, world/setting, subgenre, emotional tone and a spoiler-free storyline summary. Use this when someone asks what a book is like, what tropes it has, or what makes it tick. Uses AI (rate limited); repeat requests are cached. If the daily AI budget is spent, returns Open Library details and subjects only, with dna set to null.

tool.name: recommend_by_tropes
tool.title: Recommend books by tropes
tool.description: Recommend up to 6 books built on the given tropes, in the given kind of world when a setting is named, e.g. tropes ["enemies to lovers"] with setting "fae court". Use this when the reader describes what they want rather than naming a book (use recommend for 'books like X'). Every book is verified on Open Library, and unverifiable ones are dropped. Shows a shelf of covers. Uses AI (rate limited); repeats are cached. If the daily AI budget is spent, returns books whose Open Library subjects match the tropes instead.

tropes.description: Trope names the reader wants, e.g. ["enemies to lovers", "forced proximity"]. Books that combine several of them are preferred.

setting.description: World or setting the books should take place in, e.g. "fae court", "Victorian London", "space station". Leave it out to recommend on tropes alone.

_published_faq.name: How do I add BookDNA to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add BookDNA to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://calm-wave-h30fs.run.mcp-use.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is BookDNA MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, BookDNA scores 97/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is BookDNA's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, BookDNA scores 94/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 4 of 4 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to BookDNA?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to BookDNA in search-research on the Manufact MCP catalog include Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns, common-practice, GDELT Cloud, Lyon, and Exa.
